entries.who_files: Each domestic filing entity and registered foreign entity. The statute does not name entity types such as corporations or LLCs.
entries.due_rule: Each calendar year by the last day of the entity's anniversary month: the month its formation became effective with the Division or, for a foreign entity, the month its authority to conduct affairs in Utah took effect. It may be filed up to 60 days before that date. The Division may set a different period by rule.

sources.name: Utah Legislature — Utah Code § 16-1a-212, Annual report for division (Effective 10/1/2026)

states.draft_differences: The due rule matches: last day of the anniversary month, up to 60 days early, and the Division may set another period by rule. The draft says 'corporations, LLCs'; the statute says 'domestic filing entity'. The draft's claim that a domestic entity more than 60 days late can be administratively dissolved (§ 16-1a-602) is NOT on this page and was not verified.

evidence.filing_name: § 13.1-775 . Annual report of domestic and foreign corporations.
evidence.who_files: Each domestic corporation, and each foreign corporation authorized to transact business in the Commonwealth

entries.who_files: Domestic corporations and foreign corporations authorized to transact business in Virginia
entries.due_rule: Each year on or before the last day of the month in which the corporation was incorporated or authorized in Virginia (stated as the last day of the twelfth month after that month, then the same date each year). It can be filed no earlier than three months before the due date. The State Corporation Commission can move a due date by 1 to 11 months.

entries.filing_name: Annual registration fee (Code of Virginia § 13.1-1062), payment only
entries.who_files: Domestic LLCs, protected series, and foreign LLCs and foreign protected series registered in Virginia
entries.due_rule: Each year on or before the last day of the month in which the LLC was organized or registered in Virginia (stated as the last day of the twelfth month after that month, then the same date each year). Different dates apply to LLCs created by conversion or domestication. The Commission can move a due date by 1 to 11 months.
entries.fee: $50 per year

states.draft_differences: Unverified draft claims: the corporate annual registration fee and its due date, automatic termination of a corporation that has not filed and paid by the end of the fourth month after, and automatic cancellation of an LLC by the end of the third month after. entries.who_files: All domestic and foreign business entities
entries.due_rule: Due by the last day of the month in which the business was originally formed or registered. It can be filed up to 180 days before that date, and filing early does not change the expiration date.
entries.consequence: Not filing on or before the expiration date puts the business in delinquent status and may lead to administrative dissolution.

evidence.filing_name: Domestic Entity Annual Report Due Dates
evidence.who_files: Annual reports are required for the following entity types:
evidence.due_rule: during the calendar year quarter in which the anniversary date of the registration occurs
evidence.consequence: the entity runs the risk of being administratively dissolved

entries.who_files: Domestic business corporations (Ch. 180), nonstock corporations (Ch. 181), LLCs (Ch. 183), cooperatives (Ch. 185), LLPs (Ch. 178), LPs (Ch. 179, from 1/1/23), common law trusts (Ch. 226) and agricultural associations (Ch. 100.23)
entries.due_rule: Due each year after the calendar year of registration, during the calendar quarter containing the registration anniversary date; due by the last day of that quarter (March 31, June 30, September 30 or December 31).
entries.consequence: An entity that does not file goes delinquent; if not cured for an extended period it risks administrative dissolution. Entities that fail to file for several years are typically administratively dissolved.

evidence.filing_name: Foreign Entity Annual Report Due Date
evidence.who_files: A foreign entity registered to transact business in this state
evidence.due_rule: during the first calendar quarter of each year following the calendar year
evidence.consequence: within four months of the March 31st due date, are subject to having their Certificate

entries.who_files: Foreign entities registered to transact business in Wisconsin
entries.due_rule: Due during the first calendar quarter (by March 31) of each year after the calendar year in which the foreign entity registered.
entries.consequence: Foreign entities that have not filed within four months of the March 31 due date may have their Certificate of Authority/Registration revoked or terminated.

entries.who_files: Corporations, LLCs, LPs, RLLPs and SFs (statutory trusts have their own date)
entries.due_rule: Due on the first day of the anniversary month of the initial filing each year. For example, an entity first filed on May 15 is due May 1 each year. Statutory trust annual reports are due by January 1 each year.
